incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: latency SLO breach on /v1/stream (p95 & p99). Auto-paging on-call. Detected at 2024-11-02T14:02:03Z

maya (oncall): I'm taking this. seeing p95 -> ~820ms (baseline 80-120ms), p99 -> ~2.6s. Streaming stalls reported by multiple customers.

sam: I can confirm in metrics dashboard — recent spike aligns with a deployment around 13:45 UTC that touched prefix-hash logic for cache keys. Hit rate for prefix cache dropped from 91% to 12% after that deploy.

chris: which deploy was that? can we ID the PR?

devon: PR #4218 merged 13:43 UTC — changed prefix hashing to use murmur3 64 -> rolling hash to improve distribution across shards. It also adjusted TTL semantics (shortened default to 30s).

maya (oncall): that matches timeline. stack traces show more KV misses and additional backend paging to disk for KV caches. Those extra fetches are causing streaming stalls — evidenced by stalled first-byte times in traces.

sam: customer-impact: 3 enterprise customers (acme, finco, edusys) reporting streaming stalls and partial response hangs. Support thread opened.

support-bot: Support ticket IDs linked: S-9123, S-9124. Customers reporting token streaming stalls and occasional 502s when background fetches time out.

chris: quick triage plan: 1) rollback the prefix-hash change (if safe) 2) increase TTL temporarily to allow warm cache 3) route affected traffic to warm pool (dedicated) or fallback model variant 4) follow up with a proper patch for hashing + TTL.

maya (oncall): Agreed. I'll request rollback. @deploy-bot can you start a rollback of PR #4218 to staging first, then prod if green?

deploy-bot: Rollback job initiated for PR #4218 -> staging (job id 88412). Notifying CI.

sam: while rollback runs, let's run a quick probe to estimate rewarming time if we just bump TTL. If hit rate is 12% now, and we bump TTL from 30s -> 10m, warm pool should recover in ~3-8 minutes depending on QPS.

devon: quick metric dump:
```
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.12
prefix_cache.requests_per_min: 3200
backend.kv.latency.p95: 240ms -> 980ms
streaming.first_byte.delay.p95: 1.1s -> 4.7s
```

maya (oncall): Rolling TTL bump to 10m on prefix cache for all regions as an emergency mitigation. Making the change via runtime config now.

chris: please also add a temporary exception to prefix-hash rotation so new keys don't invalidate warm entries during rollback window.

maya (oncall): Applied runtime config: prefix_cache.ttl_override=600s. prefix_hash.rotation.disabled=true (temp). Propagating.

incident-bot: Runtime config changes applied by maya at 2024-11-02T14:15:46Z.

sam: monitoring: hit rate climbing to 38% after TTL bump, streaming stalls reduced in traces. p95 down to ~320ms, p99 trending down.

devon: rollback to staging passed smoke tests. Prod rollback scheduled and queued. Deploy bot will run canary 10% traffic first.

deploy-bot: Prod rollback (PR #4218) initiated. Canary: 10% -> 25% -> 100%. Watch windows: 3m each.

chris: if canary looks good, approve full rollback. also capture a flame graph for KV backend during canary to ensure no hidden regressions.

maya (oncall): canary at 10% now. initial telemetry looks good. no new 502s on canary, hit rate on canary nodes ~87%.

sam: canary -> 25% now. p95 on canary nodes ~110ms. main cluster still slightly noisy but improving due to TTL bump.

devon: note to postmortem later: the issue was two-fold — a hash rotation that changed key distribution + TTL reduction that made cold miss penalty visible; combined they triggered cascading backend fetches and paging. Need better rollout guard for cache key changes and perf shadow testing.

maya (oncall): Rolling full rollback to prod now.

deploy-bot: Rollback to prod complete at 2024-11-02T14:43:12Z.

sam: immediate post-rollback metrics: global prefix_cache.hit_rate -> 89%. streaming.first_byte.delay.p95 -> 95ms. p99 -> 260ms. customer tickets from S-9123/S-9124 note improvement.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers with ETA and mitigation summary.

chris: assigning follow-ups:
- sam: own postmortem and root cause analysis (include perf tests + rollout checklist)
- devon: create canary test that simulates prefix hash rotation under load and measures hit-rate/regression risk
- maya: verify alerts thresholds and add a synthetic test for streaming stalls that triggers before SLO breach

maya (oncall): Oncall handoff at 15:00 UTC to chris. I'll leave notes in the incident doc.

chris: I'll take over and keep an eye for regressions. Good triage everyone. We'll keep this thread for postmortem drafts. :thumbsup:
_meta: Generated Slack thread representing an incident about prefix cache regressions, latency spikes, and live mitigation coordination. All messages are in chronological order and formatted as single continuous thread string with sender prefixes.
